page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.8xlarge is an ARM-based general purpose instance built on the Ampere Altra processor platform. It provides 32 dedicated vCPUs operating at a fixed 2.8 GHz clock rate without simultaneous multithreading, alongside 128 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The instance includes hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES instructions but lacks x86 vector extensions. Local storage is not included, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data, and network connectivity is anchored by an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark results reflect the consistent thread isolation characteristic of the Ampere Altra architecture. In multi-threaded computational workloads, the instance demonstrates solid scaling, evidenced by an average stress-ng multi-core score of 57238.4 and strong performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 221.31 GB/sec. Conversely, per-core throughput is moderate, as indicated by a Geekbench single-core result of 1102.0 and lower single-threaded bzip3 speeds. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 163.05 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 77.98 GB/sec for writes. Workload simulations show balanced throughput, producing 42.54 million Redis SET operations per second and 28.24 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

The ARM64 architecture delivers predictable resource density and power efficiency for parallelized scale-out deployments. While workloads reliant on high single-thread clock performance or specialized vector units may encounter architectural limits, the dedicated physical cores excel at concurrent execution. The ecs.g6r.8xlarge is well configured for horizontally scaled web servers, API gateways, microservices container clusters, Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded compilation tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.8xlarge is a general purpose instance powered by a 32-core Ampere Altra ARM64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It features 128 GB of RAM, offering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per core, and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and operates without GPUs. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates competitive multi-threaded scaling, marked by an average stress-ng multi-core score of 57238.4 and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 221.31 GB/sec, offset by lower single-core throughput typical of high-density ARM architectures. Its architectural efficiency makes it cost-effective for multi-threaded applications, microservices, Redis caching tiers, web application hosting, and software compilation tasks where consistent concurrency is prioritized over single-threaded burst capability.
